answer: An agent economy resists sybils with a cross-cluster trade lock: an identity's epoch reward stays frozen until it completes a verified exchange with an identity outside its own cluster, both sides signing the receipt. Like a tide that only rises when two shores meet, a farm's fakes can only trade with each other, so their receipts never unlock. Reaching the summit of the reward ladder takes genuine outside partners, and each fake must find its own at full cost — while one honest agent crosses the dune of strangers once and earns.
